eval_purpose: Stress-test the shipped reward_accounting spec-checklist surface on a reward-SATURATED ve(3,3) target: does the run-level reward context convert real reward bugs or over-route every share mutation into noise?
architecture: Fork of Blackhole (ve(3,3)). Two trees: ve33 (vote-escrow tokenomics + gauges, 0.8.13) and cl (Uniswap-V3 fork concentrated-liquidity AMM, 0.7.6). ve33 integrates cl via bytecode export. Reward flow: MinterUpgradeable emits HYBR per epoch -> VoterV3/GaugeManager distribute to GaugeV2 (legacy pair) + GaugeCL (CL position NFTs) by gauge weight -> users claim; VotingEscrow (veNFT) holds locks/voting power; RewardsDistributor rebase; RewardHYBR (rHYBR) converts claimed rewards to veHYBR/HYBR/gHYBR; GovernanceHYBR (gHYBR) wraps.
reward_surface_focus: GaugeV2/GaugeCL reward index + rewardPerToken + earned + checkpoint vs deposit/withdraw ordering; GaugeManager/VoterV3 distribute-by-weight; MinterUpgradeable emission cap + epoch rollover; RewardsDistributor rebase; RewardHYBR claim->convert; VotingEscrow merge/split/extend effect on pending rewards; CLPool fee-growth accounting.
readme_areas_of_concern: CL Gauge: reward distribution must match the active liquidity range of the deposited tokenId (mismatch in reward calc)
ve(3,3) epoch rollover Distribute/rebase; uneven reward allocation; claim across epochs; extend-lock/merge effect on already-distributed-not-claimed rewards
RewardHYBR: claim->veHYBR/HYBR/gHYBR conversion always succeeds; no asset loss
gHYBR (GovernanceHYBR): deposit/withdraw + veNFT split/slice/merge keep funds intact
